sources.title: Lateral reading and the nature of expertise: Reading less and learning more when evaluating digital information

authors: Association of College and Research Libraries
sources.title: Framework for Information Literacy for Higher Education

concepts.definition: Judging an unfamiliar source by checking what independent sources say about it.
Stop, investigate the source, find better coverage, trace claims to the original.
Original material such as a study, dataset, law or first-hand account.

questions.q: Who took part in the Wineburg and McGrew (2019) study, and who did best?
questions.a: 10 fact checkers, 10 PhD historians and 25 Stanford students; the fact checkers, who read laterally.

questions.q: Why can a checklist like CRAAP be fooled?
questions.a: It is usually applied by examining the site itself, which a professional-looking misleading site can satisfy.

questions.q: Rank a meta-analysis, a single observational study and a testimonial by strength of evidence.
questions.a: Meta-analysis strongest, observational study weaker (association only), testimonial weakest.
